title: The crossing sample point never falls below its own base point a
statement: For a, c, delta with 0 < delta: a <= a + ofNat(crossingIndex a c delta)*ofRat delta -- samplePt (the SAME closed term crossingSampleUpper/crossingSampleLower use) never falls BELOW its own base point a. Needs only 0 < delta -- no a <= c hypothesis at all, unlike CReal.crossingLower: crossingIndex embeds as a nonnegative Nat regardless of c's position, and delta > 0 makes the product nonnegative too (via CReal.mul_nonneg), the same shape integral.rs's riemannSum_sample_in_bounds already proves for an ordinary mesh sample. This is HALF of crossingClose's domain-membership hypothesis pair; the other half, samplePt <= b, is discharged nowhere in this prelude for the general case -- see CReal.crossingCloseClamped (this batch) for how the CLAMPED construction routes around that gap instead of closing it.

formal.statement: theorem CReal.crossingSampleGeA : ((x0 : CReal) -> ((x1 : CReal) -> ((x2 : Rat) -> ((x3 : Rat.lt Rat.zero x2) -> CReal.le x0 (CReal.add x0 (CReal.mul (CReal.ofNat (CReal.bucketIndex (CReal.mul (CReal.ofRat (Rat.inv x2)) (CReal.add x1 (CReal.neg x0))) AxNat.zero)) (CReal.ofRat x2)))))))
